claim: Graziani (2024, 'Time Series Reversal: An End-of-the-Month Perspective', SSRN/job-market-paper PDF, csef.it) defines the end-of-month reversal signal as the S&P 500 return from the 4th Friday's close to the month-end close (rw=4,t) and the simple rule-of-thumb strategy (TSR: buy next month iff rw=4,t<0) outperforms buy-and-hold over a 45-year window (Jan 1975-Dec 2019 main sample, extended to Dec 1950-Dec 2023 as a robustness check). Its own robustness appendix (A.1.4) tests using the return from 1, 2, or 3 weeks before month-end (rw=1..3) instead of the 4th-Friday week and finds only the last week (rw=4) and daily returns within it (t-4..t-1) have predictive power -- 2-3 week-earlier formation windows do not. Section 2.4 reports a magnitude/precision-scaled variant (TSR-TV, weight = 1-month-ahead forecast / trailing quarterly variance, weight in [-1,2]) with Sharpe 0.588 vs. the simple TSR's 0.384 and S&P's 0.308 (Apr 1986-Dec 2019); trading-cost appendix A.1.3 finds breakeven cost ~16bp/transaction vs. typical index costs of 3-9bp/yr. Section 2.5 replicates on DOW (pattern holds) and Russell 2000 (no clear pattern); QQQ/Nasdaq-100 is not tested in the paper.
quote: outperforms the buy and hold strategy over a 45-year window
market_and_period: S&P 500 (also DOW, Russell 2000), primary sample Jan 1975-Dec 2019, extended robustness sample Dec 1950-Dec 2023.
applicability: Directly grounds E0 (base) and, via the paper's own robustness appendices, the formation-window variants E1/E2 (source's own A.1.4 test argues against widening the formation window -- documented as a headwind, not support, for E1/E2), the magnitude-scaling variant E7 (directly modeled on the paper's own TSR-TV, Sharpe 0.588 vs simple TSR's 0.384, its single largest reported improvement), and notes QQQ (E4) and partial-month holding (E5/E6) are NOT paper-tested extensions, disclosed as such rather than misattributed to the source.
limitations: Job-market-paper PDF (pre-publication), not the final peer-reviewed SSRN version (abstract page https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4349253 was located but the PDF itself was fetched from the author's own university page, csef.it, which mirrors the same working paper); TSR-TV allows leverage up to 2x and short-selling down to -1x, so its 0.588 Sharpe is not directly comparable to this round's long-only, no-leverage E7 magnitude-scaled variant (min(1, |r|/2%)), a deliberately simplified long-only analog.
independent_replication: harbourfrontquant.substack.com's secondary summary (separate source card graziani2024_eom_reversal_harbourfrontquant_summary) independently corroborates the exact rule and the '45-year' outperformance claim from the same paper.
impact_on_spec: E1/E2 (5/10-session formation) are preregistered per the owner's brief despite the source's own robustness check suggesting they may underperform E0; E7 (magnitude scaling) is the variant with the strongest source-level grounding (the paper's own best-performing TSR-TV refinement); E4 (QQQ) and E5/E6 (partial-month holding) are owner/brief-directed extensions beyond what the source itself tests, disclosed as such.

quote: negatively correlated with returns in the following month
market_and_period: S&P 500, secondary summary of Graziani (2024)'s 45-year sample.
applicability: Same claim already used to ground EOM_REVERSAL_SPY in batch-2's candidate-manifest.json (h20260928_05_registry_etf_batch2); re-verified here with a fresh snapshot and quote binding for this iteration's own direction-review.json, since batch-2's own sources/ folder never actually snapshotted this page (checked: it only has federalreserve/hulltactical/quantseeker/sec-edgar files) even though batch-2's external-brief.json cited it -- a gap in the prior round's dossier hygiene, corrected here rather than carried forward.
limitations: Secondary blog summary; does not itself give quantified CAGR/Sharpe/drawdown numbers (those come from the primary Graziani PDF, separate source card graziani2024_ssrn_eom_reversal_primary_tsrtv, and from this round's own screen_batch.py run).
independent_replication: Corroborated directly by opening the primary Graziani (2024) PDF itself in this round (source card graziani2024_ssrn_eom_reversal_primary_tsrtv), which states the identical 4th-Friday-to-month-end rule and the same 45-year outperformance claim.
impact_on_spec: Confirms E0's exact rule is unchanged from batch-2's EOM_REVERSAL_SPY; no parameter in E0 is newly invented in this round.

claim: Quantpedia's 'Front-Running Seasonality in US Stock Sectors' page (9 Select Sector SPDRs XLB/XLE/XLF/XLI/XLK/XLP/XLU/XLV/XLY, Nov 2000-Nov 2023 backtest with data through Sep 2024) tests holding 1 through 7 ETFs long-only, monthly rebalance, and reports holding TWO ETFs in long positions is the best-performing cut of the 'front-running' variant (score-window shifted forward by one month vs. the naive 'true seasonality' baseline, which is 'at best, comparable to those of the benchmark' and explicitly called inefficient). Short positions were tested but found ineffective and dropped. The page does NOT test: a 2-month shift, inverse-volatility weighting, multi-year score averaging, or adding XLC/XLRE to the 9-sector universe.
quote: holding two ETFs in long positions
market_and_period: 9 Select Sector SPDR ETFs, Nov 2000-Nov 2023 backtest window, Yahoo Finance data through Sep 5 2024.
applicability: Directly grounds S0 (base, top-2, 1-month shift) and S1/S2 (top-1/top-3, both explicitly tested by the source, top-2 was its own best pick) and S6 (shift-0 = the source's own 'true seasonality' baseline, explicitly reported by the source as failing -- preregistered here as an owner-directed robustness re-check, not because the source suggests it will pass). S_shift2, S_avg3/S_avg5, S_11sectors, S_invvol, S_absfilter are brief-directed extensions the source itself does not test, disclosed as such in candidate-manifest.json rather than misattributed.
limitations: Quantpedia's own numeric tables (CAGR/Sharpe/Calmar) are chart images, not machine-readable text in the fetched page; only qualitative claims ('more favorable Sharpe', 'higher Calmar', 'outperforms... particularly since 2009') are text-extractable. Author explicitly flags a seasonality-of-the-strategy chart (Oct-Apr / quarter-start clustering) as possibly coincidental.
independent_replication: Allocate Smartly independently tested the closely-related country-ETF front-running-seasonality mechanism (source card allocatesmartly_country_etf_front_running_extended_test) and found it failed when extended before the original author's sample window; Allocate Smartly's own article states the US-sector version specifically (this same Quantpedia page) was only on their 'todo list' and was not found to have been completed as of this fetch -- so no direct third-party replication of the sector version itself exists yet, only of the same author's closely related country-ETF version.
impact_on_spec: S1 (top-1) and S2 (top-3) are the source's own tested variants (it tested 1-7 and picked 2 as best); S6 (shift-0) is the source's own explicitly-reported-as-failing baseline, preregistered as a re-check not an expected win. S3avg/S5avg/S_shift2/S_11sectors/S_invvol/S_absfilter are new, not source-tested.

claim: Allocate Smartly independently extended Quantpedia's front-running seasonality mechanism (applied to 23 country ETFs / MSCI country indices, not the 9 US sector SPDRs) back to 1971 using ~30+ additional years of MSCI index data beyond the original author's sample, and found the strategy 'would not have been consistently effective over the long-term' in that extended pre-sample period; they explicitly state they 'will not be tracking this strategy on an ongoing basis' as a result, despite the in-sample cut reporting a Sharpe of 0.46 vs. a 0.38 benchmark (CAGR 13.2% vs 11.2%, max drawdown -59.1%).
quote: we will not be tracking this strategy on an ongoing basis
market_and_period: 23 country ETFs / MSCI country indices, extended sample back to 1971 (vs. the original author's shorter sample).
applicability: Negative-evidence caution for the whole front-running-seasonality mechanism family (S0-S9): a closely related implementation (same 'front-running' shift idea, different universe -- country ETFs, not US sectors) failed an independent out-of-sample extension by a third party with no financial interest in the result. Cited in direction-review.json's negative_experiments_checked; not a direct refutation of the sector-SPDR version (Allocate Smartly's own article states the sector version was only on their todo list, not completed), but the closest independent replication attempt found for this mechanism family and a reason this round selects conservatively (K1(b)'s contaminated-window Sharpe-drop guard plus per-family DSR) rather than accepting any 2024-2026-passing variant uncritically.
limitations: Different universe (country ETFs vs. the 9 US sector SPDRs actually used by S0-S9) and a different underlying data source (MSCI indices vs. Alpaca SIP sector-ETF daily bars); the -59.1% max drawdown reported for the in-sample cut is itself a red flag for this mechanism family regardless of the extended-sample finding.
independent_replication: None found beyond this single Allocate Smartly test; the US-sector-SPDR version itself has no known independent replication (own article confirms it was still on Allocate Smartly's to-do list as of this fetch).
impact_on_spec: Motivates treating any S-family variant's 2024-2026 outperformance skeptically; the preregistered replacement rule's stress-window Sharpe requirement (must not exceed the base by relying on the same recent-only edge) and per-family DSR are the direct response, not a new gate invented after seeing results.
